\section[la tolerancia]{la tolerancia — the tolerance}

\label{lesson:ES-C610-tolerancia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to face, then the Spanish for to persevere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la tolerancia}
\textbf{la tolerancia} — \textquotedblleft{}the tolerance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La tolerancia es importante en una sociedad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tolerance is important in a society.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tolerante} — tolerant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tolerancia} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tolerantia} 'endurance', built on \emph{tolerare} 'to bear' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la tolerancia}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to face, then the Spanish for to persevere, then say \emph{la tolerancia} again
\end{itemize}

\section[tolerar]{tolerar — to tolerate, to put up with}

\label{lesson:ES-C610-tolerar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to persevere, then the Spanish for the tolerance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: tolerar}
\textbf{tolerar} — \textquotedblleft{}to tolerate, to put up with\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No tolero las mentiras.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I do not tolerate lies.}
\end{quote}

Close to \emph{aguantar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tolerar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{tolerare} 'to carry, to endure' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la integración}
\textbf{la integración} — \textquotedblleft{}the integration\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La integración de los inmigrantes lleva tiempo.
\end{quote}

\end{quote}

\emph{Integrarse} — to fit in.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{integración} is built on \emph{integrar}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{integrare} 'to make whole', from \emph{integer} 'whole, untouched' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

Before the new one: say the Spanish for to tolerate, then the Spanish for the integration.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la inmigración}
\textbf{la inmigración} — \textquotedblleft{}the immigration\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\emph{El inmigrante} — the immigrant.

\emph{inmigración} is a learned word built on Latin \emph{immigrare} 'to move into', from \emph{migrare} 'to move house' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[la convivencia]{la convivencia — the living together, the coexistence}

\label{lesson:ES-C610-convivencia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the integration, then the Spanish for the immigration.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la convivencia}
\textbf{la convivencia} — \textquotedblleft{}the living together, the coexistence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La convivencia en el barrio es buena.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{People get on well together in the neighbourhood.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Las normas de convivencia} — the rules for living together.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{convivencia} is built on \emph{convivir}, a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{convivere} 'to live together', from \emph{vivere} 'to live' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
